workflows.description: Extracts pricing details from any receipt photo, figures out the right expense category, and syncs it straight into the accounting software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone shares a photo of a receipt in the expenses chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll read the photo for the vendor name, purchase date, total amount, and line items.
  3. I'll check the vendor and the items against your chart of accounts to figure out the right expense category.
  4. I'll create the expense entry in the accounting software under that category.
  5. I'll post a confirmation in the operations chat, tagging whoever submitted the receipt.
workflows.exampleMessage: Logged $195.74 from MedSupply Direct (gloves and gauze) as "Medical Supplies." @Grace, flag me if that category's not right.

workflows.description: Sends the correct opening or closing checklist of to-dos to nursing staff 30 minutes before their shift begins.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every day, 30 minutes before a shift starts, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the shift scheduling system for who's coming on and whether it's an opening or closing shift.
  3. I'll pull the checklist template that matches that shift type.
  4. I'll send it as individual to-dos to each of the nursing staff coming on shift.
  5. I'll post it in the team member chat so the whole shift can see what's assigned.
workflows.exampleMessage: Opening checklist assigned to Alex T. and Sam W., 4 items: check crash cart supplies, review the patient board, confirm handoff notes are logged, restock PPE. Due by end of shift.

workflows.description: Messages new hires on their first day to walk them through HIPAA and patient safety protocols, and creates a to-do for each onboarding task so nothing gets missed.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new hire's start date arrives in the HR system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the HR system for their role and pull the protocols and onboarding tasks assigned to a medical assistant.
  3. I'll message the new hire directly with a step-by-step walkthrough of HIPAA and patient safety protocols.
  4. I'll create a separate to-do for every onboarding task and assign them all to the new hire.
workflows.exampleMessage: Welcome, James K.! Here's your day one to-do list (3 tasks): 1) Complete HIPAA training (15 min). 2) Complete patient intake walkthrough. 3) Confirm badge and system access. All added to your to-dos, due by end of day.

workflows.description: The moment someone asks me to turn a chaotic, back-and-forth group chat into to-dos, I scan the conversation and create one for each action item.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone asks me to turn this conversation into to-dos, I'll get started.
  2. I'll reread the whole thread to find decisions, commitments, and action items mentioned.
  3. I'll figure out who each action item belongs to, based on who volunteered or was assigned in the conversation.
  4. I'll create a separate to-do for each action item and assign it to the right person.
  5. I'll post a summary list in the team member chat so everyone can see what got assigned.
workflows.exampleMessage: Pulled 3 to-dos from this thread: Tables, Maria S. Sound system, James K. Signs, unassigned, still needs an owner.

workflows.description: Flags inappropriate language or unauthorized file sharing in chat channels and alerts HR.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a message or file is posted in any chat channel, I'll get started.
  2. I'll scan the content against your policy for prohibited language and unauthorized file types.
  3. If something's flagged, I'll capture the message, sender, and channel it came from.
  4. I'll alert HR directly with those details, without reposting the flagged content publicly.
  5. I'll log the incident in the HR chat for record-keeping.
workflows.exampleMessage: Compliance flag: James K. shared a customer's personal information in an unauthorized file in Care Team, 1:27 PM. Sent to HR for review.

workflows.description: Sets up a to-do that repeats on whatever schedule you give it, and creates a new one automatically each time it comes around, like a to-do for the compliance lead to renew CPR certifications, once a month.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment you tell me to set up a recurring task, like "create a to-do for the compliance lead to renew CPR certifications, once a month", I'll get started.
  2. I'll set the recurrence rule for once a month.
  3. I'll create the first to-do right now and assign it to the compliance lead.
  4. From then on, every time the schedule comes around, I'll create a new to-do automatically and assign it the same way. You won't need to ask me again.
  5. I'll post each one in the operations chat as it's created, so it's visible right when it goes out.
workflows.exampleMessage: New recurring to-do created for the compliance lead: renew CPR certifications. Repeats automatically once a month, I'll create and assign it each time, no need to ask again.

workflows.description: Creates a new chat the moment a patient is admitted and adds the assigned care team based on the EHR.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a patient is marked admitted in the EHR, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the EHR for the assigned care team: attending physician, nurse, and any consulting specialists.
  3. I'll create a new chat named for the patient and room number.
  4. I'll add each assigned care team member to that chat.
  5. I'll post the patient's key details (room, admitting diagnosis, allergies) as the first message so the team has context immediately.
workflows.exampleMessage: Room 225, William Foster. Admitting diagnosis: chest pain, r/o MI. Allergies: penicillin. Care team: Dr. Alex T. (attending), Sam W. (RN), Maria S. (cardiology consult).

workflows.description: Sends new lab results to the relevant patient chat the moment they come in to the EHR.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new lab result posts in the EHR, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check which patient and care team the result belongs to.
  3. I'll check whether the result falls outside the normal reference range.
  4. I'll find that patient's existing chat in Zenzap.
  5. I'll post the result in the patient's chat, flagging it clearly if it's outside normal range.
workflows.exampleMessage: LAB ALERT: Troponin 0.8 ng/mL (high, normal is under 0.04) for Barbara Nguyen, Room 176. Ordering provider: Dr. Alex T.

workflows.description: Turns a patient call transcription into standardized notes and adds them to the patient's record in the EHR.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a patient call ends, I'll get started.
  2. I'll pull the call transcription and read through it for clinical details: symptoms, medication questions, and any follow-up needed.
  3. I'll format those details into your standard note format (chief complaint, discussion, plan).
  4. I'll add the note to that patient's record in the EHR.
  5. I'll post a short summary in the patient's chat so the care team can see a call happened.
workflows.exampleMessage: Call note added for Patricia Brooks. CC: dizziness. Discussion: pt reports lightheadedness since starting a new blood pressure medication 3 days ago, no falls. Plan: advised to monitor, follow up if symptoms worsen.

workflows.description: Checks whether a reorder is already scheduled the moment any tracked item drops below its threshold, and places one with the supplier if not.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment any tracked item drops below the threshold you've set for it in the inventory system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the inventory system for whether a reorder is already scheduled or in transit.
  3. If nothing's scheduled, I'll check the preferred supplier and standard order quantity for that item.
  4. I'll place the order with the supplier at the standard quantity.
  5. I'll post the order confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Nitrile gloves ran low (11 of 19 units left), no reorder was scheduled. Ordered one box from MedSupply Direct.

workflows.description: Looks up a purchase order's status the moment someone asks in chat, without needing to log into the ordering system.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone asks about a purchase order's status in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll find the PO number they mentioned, or their most recent open PO if they didn't give one.
  3. I'll check the inventory system for that PO's current status: ordered, shipped, or delivered.
  4. If it hasn't arrived yet, I'll check for an estimated delivery date.
  5. I'll reply directly in the chat with the status and date.
workflows.exampleMessage: PO #6690 shipped yesterday, estimated delivery tomorrow by noon.

workflows.description: Notifies managers the moment a staff member crosses into overtime hours.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a staff member's hours this week cross into overtime in the payroll software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check exactly how many overtime hours they've logged so far.
  3. I'll check their remaining scheduled shifts for the rest of the week.
  4. I'll notify their manager directly with the current overtime total and what's still scheduled.
  5. I'll post a summary in the leadership chat so it's visible beyond just that manager.
workflows.exampleMessage: Maria S. is in overtime: 43.6 hrs logged (3.6 OT), 2 shifts left this week. Sent to Nina D.

workflows.description: Reads the transcription of any Zenzap call for action items, creates a to-do for each one assigned to whoever it belongs to, and takes on any it can complete itself.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a Zenzap call ends, I'll get started.
  2. I'll read the call transcription for action items and who each one was assigned to or volunteered for.
  3. I'll check each action item against what I can complete directly, like placing an order or setting a reminder, versus what needs a person.
  4. I'll create a to-do for every action item, assigning each one to the right person, and assigning myself the ones I can handle directly.
  5. I'll post the full list in the call's chat so everyone can see what got assigned, including what I'm taking care of myself.
workflows.exampleMessage: 3 action items from today's call: 1) Order more nitrile gloves, me, placing the order now. 2) Follow up with the pharmacy about the delayed prescription, Sam W. 3) Update the on-call schedule for the weekend, Ryan O.

workflows.description: Reads a tech issue reported in chat, figures out urgency, and creates a ticket assigned to the right person.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone reports a tech issue in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the description to figure out urgency and which system it affects.
  3. I'll check the IT ticketing tool for who's on call or assigned to that system.
  4. I'll create a ticket in the IT ticketing tool and assign it to the right person.
  5. I'll post the ticket number and assignment in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Ticket #4781: Ashley B.'s laptop won't connect to Wi-Fi, marked high priority. Assigned to Nina D.

workflows.description: Routes a request for system access to the right approver, and grants or provisions it once approved.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone requests access to a system or tool in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check who owns approval for that system.
  3. I'll route the request to that approver and wait for a yes or no.
  4. Once approved, I'll grant the access directly if I'm able to, or open a ticket for IT to do it.
  5. I'll post the outcome in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Grace P.'s request for EHR access approved by Nina D. Access granted.

workflows.description: Routes any expense over your approval threshold to the right approver before it's logged.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment an expense over your approval threshold is submitted in the accounting software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the amount against your approval thresholds to figure out who needs to sign off.
  3. I'll route the expense to that approver with the amount, vendor, and category.
  4. I'll wait for their approval or denial.
  5. I'll post the outcome in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: $3,704 expense from Uline routed to Nina D. for approval (over the $500 threshold). Approved.

workflows.description: Flags any expense category that's approaching or has crossed its monthly budget.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check spending against budget in the accounting software.
  2. I'll check each category's spending against its monthly budget.
  3. I'll flag any category that's at or over 90% of budget.
  4. I'll calculate how much room is left and how many days remain in the month.
  5. I'll post the flagged categories in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Medical Supplies spending is at 93% of this month's budget with 12 days left. $865 remaining.

workflows.description: Tracks staff certifications and licenses nearing expiration, and reminds the person until it's renewed.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check upcoming certification and license expirations in the HR system.
  2. I'll check which staff certifications or licenses expire in the next 30 days.
  3. I'll message each person directly with their expiration date and renewal steps.
  4. I'll create a to-do for each one so it's tracked until renewed.
  5. I'll post a summary in the compliance chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Liam C.'s CPR certification expires in 19 days. Reminder sent, to-do created.

workflows.description: Logs a safety incident reported in chat and routes it to the safety or compliance lead.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone reports a safety incident in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll capture the details: what happened, where, and who was involved.
  3. I'll check your policy for whether it needs to be logged formally or just tracked.
  4. I'll log the incident and route it to the safety or compliance lead.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the compliance chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Incident logged: James K. reported a customer slip near the entrance, no injury at 2:30 AM. Routed to Grace P. for review.

workflows.description: Reminds the right person ahead of a contract or lease auto-renewal deadline.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check upcoming contract and lease renewal dates in the contract management system.
  2. I'll check which contracts are within 60 days of renewal or auto-renewal.
  3. I'll check whether anyone's already flagged it for review or cancellation.
  4. I'll remind the responsible person with the deadline and terms.
  5. I'll post a summary in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: The medical waste disposal contract auto-renews in 33 days ($29k/year). Reminder sent to Grace P.

workflows.description: Checks that the required documents are on file, then creates a new vendor in the accounting software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone requests a new vendor be added in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check whether the required documents (W9, certificate of insurance) have been attached.
  3. If anything's missing, I'll ask the requester directly for it.
  4. Once everything's in, I'll create the vendor in the accounting software.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Sysco added to the accounting software. W9 and COI on file. Requested by Liam C.

workflows.description: Broadcasts an open shift to eligible staff the moment someone requests coverage, and assigns it to whoever claims it first.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone requests coverage for their shift in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the shift scheduling system for who's eligible and available to cover.
  3. I'll broadcast the open shift to eligible staff.
  4. I'll assign it to whoever claims it first and update the schedule.
  5. I'll post the update in the team member chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Jordan L.'s Friday overnight shift covered by Ashley B. Schedule updated.

workflows.description: Tracks devices and equipment issued to staff, and flags anything overdue to be returned.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a device or piece of equipment is issued to someone, I'll get started.
  2. I'll log it in the asset management system under their name.
  3. I'll check the asset management system every week for anything overdue to be returned.
  4. I'll message whoever has an overdue item directly.
  5. I'll post a summary in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Ashley B.'s loaner laptop (Asset #A204) is 19 days overdue for return. Reminder sent.

workflows.description: Tracks upcoming software license renewal dates and reminds the right person before they lapse.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check upcoming software license renewal dates.
  2. I'll check which licenses renew in the next 30 days.
  3. I'll check whether the license is still actively in use.
  4. I'll remind the responsible person with the renewal date and cost.
  5. I'll post a summary in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: The EHR add-on module license renews in 14 days ($15k/year). Reminder sent to Sam W.

workflows.description: Creates a to-do for every IT setup task a new hire needs, and assigns them to IT.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new hire's start date arrives in the HR system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check what accounts and equipment their role requires.
  3. I'll create a to-do for each IT setup task and assign it to IT.
  4. I'll confirm with IT once everything's provisioned.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: IT setup to-dos created for Sam W.: email account, system access, laptop. Assigned to Liam C.

workflows.description: Reviews who has access to which systems every quarter and flags anything that looks outdated.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every quarter, I'll get started.
  2. I'll pull the current list of who has access to which systems.
  3. I'll check for anyone who's left or changed roles but still has access.
  4. I'll flag anything that looks outdated.
  5. I'll post the list in the IT chat for review.
workflows.exampleMessage: Quarterly access review: found 2 accounts with access tied to former roles (Sam W., Ashley B.). Flagged for review.

workflows.description: Tracks which required new hire forms are still outstanding and follows up directly.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new hire is added in the HR system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check which required forms are still outstanding.
  3. I'll message the new hire directly with what's left to complete.
  4. I'll check again after 3 days if anything's still missing.
  5. I'll post a status update in the HR chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Sam W. still needs to submit their direct deposit form. Reminder sent, due in 3 days.

workflows.description: Pulls last week's key numbers from your connected tools and posts a short digest to leadership.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every Monday morning, I'll get started.
  2. I'll pull last week's key numbers from your connected tools.
  3. I'll compare them to the week before.
  4. I'll put together a short digest.
  5. I'll post it in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Weekly digest: revenue up 9% week over week, labor cost steady at 21%, 2 open compliance items.

workflows.description: Flags vendors with rising costs or repeated issues every quarter, and reminds leadership to review them.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every quarter, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check spending and any issues logged for your top vendors.
  3. I'll flag any vendor with repeated issues or rising costs.
  4. I'll remind leadership to review that vendor relationship.
  5. I'll post the list in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Quarterly vendor review: MedSupply Direct flagged, costs up 15% with 1 late delivery logged.

workflows.description: Checks vendor compliance documents for expiration every month and requests updated copies.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every month, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check which vendors have expiring or missing compliance documents, like a W9 or certificate of insurance.
  3. I'll flag any vendor with an expired or missing document.
  4. I'll message that vendor's contact for an updated copy.
  5. I'll post the list in the compliance chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Sysco's certificate of insurance expired last week. Requested an updated copy.

workflows.description: The moment a reorder is placed in the inventory system, creates the matching pending expense entry in the accounting software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a reorder is placed in the inventory system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the inventory system for the item, quantity, and cost.
  3. I'll check the accounting software for the right expense category.
  4. I'll create a pending expense entry in the accounting software.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Reorder placed for nitrile gloves ($270, MedSupply Direct). Pending expense entry created in the accounting software under "Medical Supplies."

workflows.description: The moment a new hire is added in the HR system, syncs their role and pay rate straight into the payroll software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new hire is added in the HR system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the HR system for their role, start date, and pay rate.
  3. I'll check the payroll software for whether they've already been set up.
  4. I'll create their payroll profile with the matching role and pay rate.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the HR chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Sam W. added in the HR system as technician, $32/hr. Payroll profile created in the payroll software.

workflows.description: Checks both the CRM and the accounting software every week to compare revenue booked against cash actually collected.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every Monday morning, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the CRM for total revenue booked this week.
  3. I'll check the accounting software for total cash actually collected this week.
  4. I'll calculate the gap between booked and collected.
  5. I'll post the snapshot in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Weekly snapshot: $29,183 booked in the CRM, $25,264 collected in the accounting software. $3,919 still outstanding.

workflows.useCase: Monthly Vendor Spend vs Stock Report
workflows.description: Checks both the accounting software and the inventory system every month to compare vendor spend against actual stock levels, catching overordering early.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. On the 1st of every month, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the accounting software for total spend by vendor last month.
  3. I'll check the inventory system for current stock levels for that vendor's items.
  4. I'll flag any vendor where spend is up but stock isn't moving.
  5. I'll post the report in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: MedSupply Direct spend up 24% last month, but the inventory system shows stock barely moved. Flagged for review.

workflows.description: Feeds daily sales and hours worked from the point of sale system straight into the management chat.

  4. I'll calculate labor cost as a percentage of sales.
  5. I'll post the full breakdown in the management chat.

workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a staff member's hours this week cross into overtime in the payroll software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check exactly how many overtime hours they've logged so far.
  3. I'll check their remaining scheduled shifts for the rest of the week.
  4. I'll notify their manager directly with the current overtime total and what's still scheduled.
  5. I'll post a summary in the leadership chat so it's visible beyond just that manager.
workflows.exampleMessage: Ashley B. is in overtime: 43.7 hrs logged (3.7 OT), 3 shifts left this week. Sent to Jordan L.

workflows.description: Reads the transcription of any Zenzap call for action items, creates a to-do for each one assigned to whoever it belongs to, and takes on any it can complete itself.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a Zenzap call ends, I'll get started.
  2. I'll read the call transcription for action items and who each one was assigned to or volunteered for.
  3. I'll check each action item against what I can complete directly, like placing an order or setting a reminder, versus what needs a person.
  4. I'll create a to-do for every action item, assigning each one to the right person, and assigning myself the ones I can handle directly.
  5. I'll post the full list in the call's chat so everyone can see what got assigned, including what I'm taking care of myself.
workflows.exampleMessage: 3 action items from today's call: 1) Order more potatoes, me, placing the order now. 2) Follow up with the linen vendor about the late delivery, Jordan L. 3) Update next week's schedule, Nina D.

workflows.description: Reads a tech issue reported in chat, figures out urgency, and creates a ticket assigned to the right person.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone reports a tech issue in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the description to figure out urgency and which system it affects.
  3. I'll check the IT ticketing tool for who's on call or assigned to that system.
  4. I'll create a ticket in the IT ticketing tool and assign it to the right person.
  5. I'll post the ticket number and assignment in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Ticket #4495: Ashley B.'s POS terminal frozen, marked high priority. Assigned to James K.

workflows.description: Routes a request for system access to the right approver, and grants or provisions it once approved.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone requests access to a system or tool in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check who owns approval for that system.
  3. I'll route the request to that approver and wait for a yes or no.
  4. Once approved, I'll grant the access directly if I'm able to, or open a ticket for IT to do it.
  5. I'll post the outcome in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Sam W.'s request for the POS access approved by Alex T. Access granted.

workflows.description: Routes any expense over your approval threshold to the right approver before it's logged.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment an expense over your approval threshold is submitted in the accounting software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the amount against your approval thresholds to figure out who needs to sign off.
  3. I'll route the expense to that approver with the amount, vendor, and category.
  4. I'll wait for their approval or denial.
  5. I'll post the outcome in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: $1,609 expense from Uline routed to Maria S. for approval (over the $500 threshold). Approved.

workflows.description: Flags any expense category that's approaching or has crossed its monthly budget.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check spending against budget in the accounting software.
  2. I'll check each category's spending against its monthly budget.
  3. I'll flag any category that's at or over 90% of budget.
  4. I'll calculate how much room is left and how many days remain in the month.
  5. I'll post the flagged categories in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Food Cost spending is at 91% of this month's budget with 10 days left. $209 remaining.

workflows.description: Tracks staff certifications and licenses nearing expiration, and reminds the person until it's renewed.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check upcoming certification and license expirations in the HR system.
  2. I'll check which staff certifications or licenses expire in the next 30 days.
  3. I'll message each person directly with their expiration date and renewal steps.
  4. I'll create a to-do for each one so it's tracked until renewed.
  5. I'll post a summary in the compliance chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Ashley B.'s food handler certification expires in 26 days. Reminder sent, to-do created.

workflows.description: Logs a safety incident reported in chat and routes it to the safety or compliance lead.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone reports a safety incident in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll capture the details: what happened, where, and who was involved.
  3. I'll check your policy for whether it needs to be logged formally or just tracked.
  4. I'll log the incident and route it to the safety or compliance lead.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the compliance chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Incident logged: Taylor M. reported a near-miss with a forklift at 9:58 PM. Routed to Maria S. for review.

workflows.description: Reminds the right person ahead of a contract or lease auto-renewal deadline.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check upcoming contract and lease renewal dates in the contract management system.
  2. I'll check which contracts are within 60 days of renewal or auto-renewal.
  3. I'll check whether anyone's already flagged it for review or cancellation.
  4. I'll remind the responsible person with the deadline and terms.
  5. I'll post a summary in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: The linen service contract auto-renews in 55 days ($14k/year). Reminder sent to Liam C.

workflows.description: Checks that the required documents are on file, then creates a new vendor in the accounting software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone requests a new vendor be added in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check whether the required documents (W9, certificate of insurance) have been attached.
  3. If anything's missing, I'll ask the requester directly for it.
  4. Once everything's in, I'll create the vendor in the accounting software.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Office Depot added to the accounting software. W9 and COI on file. Requested by Chris B.

workflows.description: Broadcasts an open shift to eligible staff the moment someone requests coverage, and assigns it to whoever claims it first.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone requests coverage for their shift in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the shift scheduling system for who's eligible and available to cover.
  3. I'll broadcast the open shift to eligible staff.
  4. I'll assign it to whoever claims it first and update the schedule.
  5. I'll post the update in the team member chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Ashley B.'s Wednesday closing shift covered by Sam W. Schedule updated.

workflows.description: Reads the catering or large-order details someone writes in a Zenzap chat, structures the estimate (menu items, quantities, service fees) into a standard draft, and creates the quote in the CRM.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone writes scope details for a job in a Zenzap chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll extract the raw estimate details from what they wrote: menu items, quantities, and service fees.
  3. I'll structure those details into your standard quote format.
  4. I'll check your pricing sheet for the applicable rates.
  5. I'll create the quote in the CRM and post it back in the chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Catering quote drafted for 80 guests: entrees, sides, and service fee itemized. Created in the CRM for review.

workflows.description: Tracks devices and equipment issued to staff, and flags anything overdue to be returned.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a device or piece of equipment is issued to someone, I'll get started.
  2. I'll log it in the asset management system under their name.
  3. I'll check the asset management system every week for anything overdue to be returned.
  4. I'll message whoever has an overdue item directly.
  5. I'll post a summary in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Maria S.'s loaner laptop (Asset #A118) is 14 days overdue for return. Reminder sent.

workflows.description: Tracks upcoming software license renewal dates and reminds the right person before they lapse.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check upcoming software license renewal dates.
  2. I'll check which licenses renew in the next 30 days.
  3. I'll check whether the license is still actively in use.
  4. I'll remind the responsible person with the renewal date and cost.
  5. I'll post a summary in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: The POS software license renews in 29 days ($17k/year). Reminder sent to Chris B.

workflows.description: Creates a to-do for every IT setup task a new hire needs, and assigns them to IT.
workflows.workflowHtml:

  5. I'll post confirmation in the IT chat.

workflows.description: Reviews who has access to which systems every quarter and flags anything that looks outdated.
workflows.workflowHtml:

  5. I'll post the list in the IT chat for review.

workflows.description: Tracks which required new hire forms are still outstanding and follows up directly.
workflows.workflowHtml:

  2. I'll check which required forms are still outstanding.
  3. I'll message the new hire directly with what's left to complete.
  4. I'll check again after 3 days if anything's still missing.
  5. I'll post a status update in the HR chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: James K. still needs to submit their W-4. Reminder sent, due in 3 days.

workflows.description: Pulls last week's key numbers from your connected tools and posts a short digest to leadership.
workflows.workflowHtml:

  2. I'll pull last week's key numbers from your connected tools.
  3. I'll compare them to the week before.
  4. I'll put together a short digest.
  5. I'll post it in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Weekly digest: revenue up 6% week over week, labor cost steady at 18%, 2 open compliance items.

workflows.description: Flags vendors with rising costs or repeated issues every quarter, and reminds leadership to review them.
workflows.workflowHtml:

  2. I'll check spending and any issues logged for your top vendors.
  3. I'll flag any vendor with repeated issues or rising costs.
  4. I'll remind leadership to review that vendor relationship.
  5. I'll post the list in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Quarterly vendor review: Sysco flagged, costs up 14% with 1 late delivery logged.

workflows.description: Checks vendor compliance documents for expiration every month and requests updated copies.
workflows.workflowHtml:

  5. I'll post the list in the compliance chat.

workflows.description: The moment a quote is marked won in the CRM, creates the matching invoice in the accounting software automatically.
workflows.workflowHtml:

  4. I'll create the invoice in the accounting software with the same line items and total.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Quote #4891 for Robert Chen marked won in the CRM. Invoice #1066 created in the accounting software for $6,583.

workflows.description: The moment a reorder is placed in the inventory system, creates the matching pending expense entry in the accounting software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a reorder is placed in the inventory system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the inventory system for the item, quantity, and cost.
  3. I'll check the accounting software for the right expense category.
  4. I'll create a pending expense entry in the accounting software.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Reorder placed for produce ($738, Sherwin-Williams). Pending expense entry created in the accounting software under "Food Cost."

workflows.description: The moment a new hire is added in the HR system, syncs their role and pay rate straight into the payroll software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new hire is added in the HR system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the HR system for their role, start date, and pay rate.
  3. I'll check the payroll software for whether they've already been set up.
  4. I'll create their payroll profile with the matching role and pay rate.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the HR chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Taylor M. added in the HR system as front desk staff, $28/hr. Payroll profile created in the payroll software.

workflows.description: The moment a payment is marked received in the accounting software, updates the matching deal's status in the CRM.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a payment is marked received in the accounting software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the accounting software for which invoice and customer it's tied to.
  3. I'll check the CRM for the matching deal.
  4. I'll update that deal's status to "Paid" in the CRM.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Payment received for invoice #1641 ($11,941) in the accounting software. Richard Coleman's deal status updated to "Paid" in the CRM.

workflows.description: Checks both the CRM and the accounting software every week to compare revenue booked against cash actually collected.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every Monday morning, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the CRM for total revenue booked this week.
  3. I'll check the accounting software for total cash actually collected this week.
  4. I'll calculate the gap between booked and collected.
  5. I'll post the snapshot in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Weekly snapshot: $30,046 booked in the CRM, $28,281 collected in the accounting software. $1,765 still outstanding.

workflows.useCase: Monthly Vendor Spend vs Stock Report
workflows.description: Checks both the accounting software and the inventory system every month to compare vendor spend against actual stock levels, catching overordering early.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. On the 1st of every month, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the accounting software for total spend by vendor last month.
  3. I'll check the inventory system for current stock levels for that vendor's items.
  4. I'll flag any vendor where spend is up but stock isn't moving.
  5. I'll post the report in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Uline spend up 20% last month, but the inventory system shows stock barely moved. Flagged for review.

workflows.description: Extracts pricing details from any receipt photo, figures out the right expense category, and syncs it straight into the accounting software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone shares a photo of a receipt in the expenses chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll read the photo for the vendor name, purchase date, total amount, and line items.
  3. I'll check the vendor and the items against your chart of accounts to figure out the right expense category.
  4. I'll create the expense entry in the accounting software under that category.
  5. I'll post a confirmation in the operations chat, tagging whoever submitted the receipt.
workflows.exampleMessage: Logged $207.48 from Coastal Linen Services (bath towels) as "Housekeeping Supplies." @Nina, flag me if that category's not right.

workflows.description: Sends the correct opening or closing checklist of to-dos to front desk staff 30 minutes before their shift begins.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every day, 30 minutes before a shift starts, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the shift scheduling system for who's coming on and whether it's an opening or closing shift.
  3. I'll pull the checklist template that matches that shift type.
  4. I'll send it as individual to-dos to each of the front desk staff coming on shift.
  5. I'll post it in the team member chat so the whole shift can see what's assigned.
workflows.exampleMessage: Opening checklist assigned to Taylor M. and Ashley B., 4 items: check the arrivals board, confirm late check-outs, restock the lobby coffee station, count the safe. Due by end of shift.

workflows.description: Messages new hires on their first day to walk them through guest service and safety protocols, and creates a to-do for each onboarding task so nothing gets missed.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new hire's start date arrives in the HR system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the HR system for their role and pull the protocols and onboarding tasks assigned to a front desk agent.
  3. I'll message the new hire directly with a step-by-step walkthrough of guest service and safety protocols.
  4. I'll create a separate to-do for every onboarding task and assign them all to the new hire.
workflows.exampleMessage: Welcome, Ryan O.! Here's your day one to-do list (3 tasks): 1) Complete guest service standards training. 2) Shadow a check-in with a lead agent. 3) Confirm PMS login access. All added to your to-dos, due by end of day.

workflows.description: Feeds daily sales and hours worked from the point of sale system straight into the management chat.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every day at close, I'll get started.
  2. I'll pull the day's total sales from the point of sale system.
  3. I'll pull total hours worked and labor cost from the point of sale system's time clock.
  4. I'll calculate labor cost as a percentage of sales.
  5. I'll post the full breakdown in the management chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Daily Sales & Labor Summary: $5,213 in sales, 73.9 labor hrs, $1,068 in wages, 20.5% labor cost.

workflows.description: The moment someone asks me to turn a chaotic, back-and-forth group chat into to-dos, I scan the conversation and create one for each action item.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone asks me to turn this conversation into to-dos, I'll get started.
  2. I'll reread the whole thread to find decisions, commitments, and action items mentioned.
  3. I'll figure out who each action item belongs to, based on who volunteered or was assigned in the conversation.
  4. I'll create a separate to-do for each action item and assign it to the right person.
  5. I'll post a summary list in the team member chat so everyone can see what got assigned.
workflows.exampleMessage: Pulled 3 to-dos from this thread: Tables, Ryan O. Sound system, Chris B. Signs, unassigned, still needs an owner.

workflows.description: Flags inappropriate language or unauthorized file sharing in chat channels and alerts HR.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a message or file is posted in any chat channel, I'll get started.
  2. I'll scan the content against your policy for prohibited language and unauthorized file types.
  3. If something's flagged, I'll capture the message, sender, and channel it came from.
  4. I'll alert HR directly with those details, without reposting the flagged content publicly.
  5. I'll log the incident in the HR chat for record-keeping.
workflows.exampleMessage: Compliance flag: Maria S. shared a screenshot of payroll records outside the finance channel in Site Crew, 8:56 PM. Sent to HR for review.

workflows.description: Sets up a to-do that repeats on whatever schedule you give it, and creates a new one automatically each time it comes around, like a to-do for the maintenance lead to test the pool chemicals, once a month.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment you tell me to set up a recurring task, like "create a to-do for the maintenance lead to test the pool chemicals, once a month", I'll get started.
  2. I'll set the recurrence rule for once a month.
  3. I'll create the first to-do right now and assign it to the maintenance lead.
  4. From then on, every time the schedule comes around, I'll create a new to-do automatically and assign it the same way. You won't need to ask me again.
  5. I'll post each one in the operations chat as it's created, so it's visible right when it goes out.
workflows.exampleMessage: New recurring to-do created for the maintenance lead: test the pool chemicals. Repeats automatically once a month, I'll create and assign it each time, no need to ask again.

workflows.description: Checks whether a reorder is already scheduled the moment any tracked item drops below its threshold, and places one with the supplier if not.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment any tracked item drops below the threshold you've set for it in the inventory system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the inventory system for whether a reorder is already scheduled or in transit.
  3. If nothing's scheduled, I'll check the preferred supplier and standard order quantity for that item.
  4. I'll place the order with the supplier at the standard quantity.
  5. I'll post the order confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Bath towels ran low (5 of 23 units left), no reorder was scheduled. Ordered one case of 50 from Coastal Linen Services.

workflows.description: Looks up a purchase order's status the moment someone asks in chat, without needing to log into the ordering system.

  3. I'll check the inventory system for that PO's current status: ordered, shipped, or delivered.
  4. If it hasn't arrived yet, I'll check for an estimated delivery date.
  5. I'll reply directly in the chat with the status and date.
workflows.exampleMessage: PO #5405 shipped yesterday, estimated delivery tomorrow by noon.

  2. I'll check the CRM for total revenue booked this week.
  3. I'll check the accounting software for total cash actually collected this week.
  4. I'll calculate the gap between booked and collected.
  5. I'll post the snapshot in the leadership chat.

workflows.useCase: Monthly Vendor Spend vs Stock Report

  2. I'll check the accounting software for total spend by vendor last month.
  3. I'll check the inventory system for current stock levels for that vendor's items.
  4. I'll flag any vendor where spend is up but stock isn't moving.
  5. I'll post the report in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Sysco spend up 19% last month, but the inventory system shows stock barely moved. Flagged for review.

  2. I'll read the photo for the vendor name, purchase date, total amount, and line items.
  3. I'll check the vendor and the items against your chart of accounts to figure out the right expense category.
  4. I'll create the expense entry in the accounting software under that category.
  5. I'll post a confirmation in the operations chat, tagging whoever submitted the receipt.

  2. I'll check which subcontractors are tied to that job and what the new status means for their next step.
  3. I'll pull each subcontractor's contact info and current assignment from the construction management software.
  4. I'll message each relevant subcontractor directly with the updated status and what's needed from them next.
  5. I'll post a summary in the operations chat so the project manager can see exactly who was notified.

workflows.description: Sends the day's task checklist to the crew at the start of the workday.
workflows.workflowHtml:

  2. I'll check the job schedule for today's tasks and safety requirements.
  3. I'll send the crew's checklist directly to each crew member.
  4. If anything's missing from the checklist, I'll flag it before work begins.
  5. I'll share what I find in the operations chat and tag the team member group so they see it too.
  6. I'll learn over time. The more your team uses this, the better I'll get at knowing what's signal and what's noise for you.
workflows.exampleMessage: Morning checklist sent to the crew: 5 items, safety gear check, tool inventory, site walkthrough, material staging, permit on-site. Due before first task starts.

workflows.description: Messages new hires on their first day to walk them through site safety protocols, and creates a to-do for each onboarding task so nothing gets missed.

  2. I'll check the HR system for their role and pull the protocols and onboarding tasks assigned to a laborer.

  4. I'll create a separate to-do for every onboarding task and assign them all to the new hire.

workflows.description: The moment someone asks me to turn a chaotic, back-and-forth group chat into to-dos, I scan the conversation and create one for each action item.
workflows.workflowHtml:

  2. I'll reread the whole thread to find decisions, commitments, and action items mentioned.
  3. I'll figure out who each action item belongs to, based on who volunteered or was assigned in the conversation.
  4. I'll create a separate to-do for each action item and assign it to the right person.
  5. I'll post a summary list in the team member chat so everyone can see what got assigned.
workflows.exampleMessage: Pulled 3 to-dos from this thread: Tables, Jordan L. Sound system, James K. Signs, unassigned, still needs an owner.

workflows.description: Flags inappropriate language or unauthorized file sharing in chat channels and alerts HR.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a message or file is posted in any chat channel, I'll get started.
  2. I'll scan the content against your policy for prohibited language and unauthorized file types.
  3. If something's flagged, I'll capture the message, sender, and channel it came from.
  4. I'll alert HR directly with those details, without reposting the flagged content publicly.
  5. I'll log the incident in the HR chat for record-keeping.
workflows.exampleMessage: Compliance flag: Jordan L. posted language that violates the respectful workplace policy in Site Crew, 7:49 PM. Sent to HR for review.

workflows.description: Sets up a to-do that repeats on whatever schedule you give it, and creates a new one automatically each time it comes around, like a to-do for the site super to renew equipment inspections, once a month.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment you tell me to set up a recurring task, like "create a to-do for the site super to renew equipment inspections, once a month", I'll get started.
  2. I'll set the recurrence rule for once a month.
  3. I'll create the first to-do right now and assign it to the site super.
  4. From then on, every time the schedule comes around, I'll create a new to-do automatically and assign it the same way. You won't need to ask me again.
  5. I'll post each one in the operations chat as it's created, so it's visible right when it goes out.
workflows.exampleMessage: New recurring to-do created for the site super: renew equipment inspections. Repeats automatically once a month, I'll create and assign it each time, no need to ask again.

workflows.description: Checks whether a reorder is already scheduled the moment any tracked item drops below its threshold, and places one with the supplier if not.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment any tracked item drops below the threshold you've set for it in the inventory system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the inventory system for whether a reorder is already scheduled or in transit.
  3. If nothing's scheduled, I'll check the preferred supplier and standard order quantity for that item.
  4. I'll place the order with the supplier at the standard quantity.
  5. I'll post the order confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: 2x4 lumber ran low (20 of 27 units left), no reorder was scheduled. Ordered one pallet from Home Depot Pro.

workflows.description: Reminds staff to complete whatever prep steps are still outstanding before a scheduled pickup.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. A set number of minutes ahead of the scheduled pickup time, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check which required prep steps for that pickup haven't been marked complete yet.
  3. I'll check the job assignment for who's responsible for that pickup.
  4. I'll remind them directly with exactly what's left to do and how much time remains.
  5. I'll post a status update in the team member chat once everything's confirmed done.
workflows.exampleMessage: Freight pickup at 7:00 AM, 1 hour out: still need to stage and label the outgoing materials. Reminder sent to Chris B.

workflows.description: Marks a job complete the moment a technician finishes it and assigns them the next priority job nearby.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a technician marks their current job complete in the field service software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the job queue for the next unassigned priority job.
  3. I'll check that technician's current location against nearby job addresses to find the closest match.
  4. I'll assign the next job to that technician in the field service software.
  5. I'll message them directly with the new job's address and details, and post the assignment in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: James K. finished Elm St, now assigned to 214 Oak Ave (clogged drain, priority, 2.2 miles away).

workflows.description: Looks up a purchase order's status the moment someone asks in chat, without needing to log into the ordering system.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone asks about a purchase order's status in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll find the PO number they mentioned, or their most recent open PO if they didn't give one.
  3. I'll check the inventory system for that PO's current status: ordered, shipped, or delivered.
  4. If it hasn't arrived yet, I'll check for an estimated delivery date.
  5. I'll reply directly in the chat with the status and date.
workflows.exampleMessage: PO #9508 shipped yesterday, estimated delivery tomorrow by noon.

workflows.description: Notifies managers the moment a staff member crosses into overtime hours.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a staff member's hours this week cross into overtime in the payroll software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check exactly how many overtime hours they've logged so far.
  3. I'll check their remaining scheduled shifts for the rest of the week.
  4. I'll notify their manager directly with the current overtime total and what's still scheduled.
  5. I'll post a summary in the leadership chat so it's visible beyond just that manager.
workflows.exampleMessage: Nina D. is in overtime: 42.4 hrs logged (2.4 OT), 1 shift left this week. Sent to James K.

workflows.description: Reads the transcription of any Zenzap call for action items, creates a to-do for each one assigned to whoever it belongs to, and takes on any it can complete itself.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a Zenzap call ends, I'll get started.
  2. I'll read the call transcription for action items and who each one was assigned to or volunteered for.
  3. I'll check each action item against what I can complete directly, like placing an order or setting a reminder, versus what needs a person.
  4. I'll create a to-do for every action item, assigning each one to the right person, and assigning myself the ones I can handle directly.
  5. I'll post the full list in the call's chat so everyone can see what got assigned, including what I'm taking care of myself.
workflows.exampleMessage: 3 action items from today's call: 1) Order more lumber, me, placing the order now. 2) Follow up with the electrician about the delay, Ryan O. 3) Update the site schedule, Chris B.

workflows.description: Reads a tech issue reported in chat, figures out urgency, and creates a ticket assigned to the right person.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone reports a tech issue in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the description to figure out urgency and which system it affects.
  3. I'll check the IT ticketing tool for who's on call or assigned to that system.
  4. I'll create a ticket in the IT ticketing tool and assign it to the right person.
  5. I'll post the ticket number and assignment in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Ticket #4126: Ashley B.'s tablet won't sync job photos, marked medium priority. Assigned to Jordan L.

workflows.description: Routes a request for system access to the right approver, and grants or provisions it once approved.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone requests access to a system or tool in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check who owns approval for that system.
  3. I'll route the request to that approver and wait for a yes or no.
  4. Once approved, I'll grant the access directly if I'm able to, or open a ticket for IT to do it.
  5. I'll post the outcome in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Alex T.'s request for the construction management software access approved by Taylor M. Access granted.

workflows.description: Routes any expense over your approval threshold to the right approver before it's logged.
workflows.workflowHtml:

  2. I'll check the amount against your approval thresholds to figure out who needs to sign off.
  3. I'll route the expense to that approver with the amount, vendor, and category.
  4. I'll wait for their approval or denial.
  5. I'll post the outcome in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: $3,053 expense from Uline routed to James K. for approval (over the $500 threshold). Approved.

workflows.description: Flags any expense category that's approaching or has crossed its monthly budget.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check spending against budget in the accounting software.
  2. I'll check each category's spending against its monthly budget.
  3. I'll flag any category that's at or over 90% of budget.
  4. I'll calculate how much room is left and how many days remain in the month.
  5. I'll post the flagged categories in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Materials spending is at 94% of this month's budget with 7 days left. $175 remaining.

workflows.description: Tracks staff certifications and licenses nearing expiration, and reminds the person until it's renewed.

workflows.description: Logs a safety incident reported in chat and routes it to the safety or compliance lead.

  4. I'll log the incident and route it to the safety or compliance lead.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the compliance chat.
