workflows.description: The moment a new hire is added in the HR system, syncs their role and pay rate straight into the payroll software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new hire is added in the HR system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the HR system for their role, start date, and pay rate.
  3. I'll check the payroll software for whether they've already been set up.
  4. I'll create their payroll profile with the matching role and pay rate.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the HR chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Chris B. added in the HR system as technician, $21/hr. Payroll profile created in the payroll software.

workflows.description: The moment parts are logged as used on a job in the field service software, deducts them from the inventory system, and reorders automatically if that drops it below threshold.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment parts are logged as used on a job in the field service software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the field service software for which parts and how many were used.
  3. I'll deduct that quantity from the inventory system.
  4. I'll check whether that drops the item below its reorder threshold.
  5. If it does, I'll place the reorder and post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Jordan L. logged 5 copper fittings used on Job #2223. Deducted from inventory system, now at 6 units, below the 10-unit threshold. Reorder placed.

workflows.description: The moment a payment is marked received in the accounting software, updates the matching deal's status in the CRM.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a payment is marked received in the accounting software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the accounting software for which invoice and customer it's tied to.
  3. I'll check the CRM for the matching deal.
  4. I'll update that deal's status to "Paid" in the CRM.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Payment received for invoice #1085 ($5,881) in the accounting software. Barbara Nguyen's deal status updated to "Paid" in the CRM.

workflows.description: The moment a job is marked complete in the field service software, updates the matching project's status in the CRM.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a job is marked complete in the field service software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the field service software for which job and customer it's tied to.
  3. I'll check the CRM for the matching project or deal.
  4. I'll update that record's status to "Completed" in the CRM.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Job #2549 marked complete in the field service software. Karen Sullivan's project status updated to "Completed" in the CRM.

workflows.description: Checks both the CRM and the accounting software every week to compare revenue booked against cash actually collected.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every Monday morning, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the CRM for total revenue booked this week.
  3. I'll check the accounting software for total cash actually collected this week.
  4. I'll calculate the gap between booked and collected.
  5. I'll post the snapshot in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Weekly snapshot: $8,923 booked in the CRM, $3,374 collected in the accounting software. $5,549 still outstanding.

workflows.useCase: Monthly Vendor Spend vs Stock Report
workflows.description: Checks both the accounting software and the inventory system every month to compare vendor spend against actual stock levels, catching overordering early.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. On the 1st of every month, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the accounting software for total spend by vendor last month.
  3. I'll check the inventory system for current stock levels for that vendor's items.
  4. I'll flag any vendor where spend is up but stock isn't moving.
  5. I'll post the report in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: BuildRight Supply spend up 15% last month, but the inventory system shows stock barely moved. Flagged for review.

workflows.description: Extracts pricing details from any receipt photo, figures out the right expense category, and syncs it straight into the accounting software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone shares a photo of a receipt in the expenses chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll read the photo for the vendor name, purchase date, total amount, and line items.
  3. I'll check the vendor and the items against your chart of accounts to figure out the right expense category.
  4. I'll create the expense entry in the accounting software under that category.
  5. I'll post a confirmation in the operations chat, tagging whoever submitted the receipt.
workflows.exampleMessage: Logged $905.18 from Uline (shipping boxes) as "Packaging Supplies." @Sam, flag me if that category's not right.

workflows.description: Sends the correct opening or closing checklist of to-dos to sales associates 30 minutes before their shift begins.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every day, 30 minutes before a shift starts, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the shift scheduling system for who's coming on and whether it's an opening or closing shift.
  3. I'll pull the checklist template that matches that shift type.
  4. I'll send it as individual to-dos to each of the sales associates coming on shift.
  5. I'll post it in the team member chat so the whole shift can see what's assigned.
workflows.exampleMessage: Closing checklist assigned to Ryan O. and Sam W., 4 items: straighten displays, count the register drawer, check the fitting rooms, restock front tables. Due by end of shift.

workflows.description: Messages new hires on their first day to walk them through register and loss prevention protocols, and creates a to-do for each onboarding task so nothing gets missed.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new hire's start date arrives in the HR system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the HR system for their role and pull the protocols and onboarding tasks assigned to a sales associate.
  3. I'll message the new hire directly with a step-by-step walkthrough of register and loss prevention protocols.
  4. I'll create a separate to-do for every onboarding task and assign them all to the new hire.
workflows.exampleMessage: Welcome, Alex T.! Here's your day one to-do list (3 tasks): 1) Complete register training. 2) Complete loss prevention walkthrough. 3) Shadow a shift lead for one hour. All added to your to-dos, due by end of day.

workflows.description: Feeds daily sales and hours worked from the point of sale system straight into the management chat.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every day at close, I'll get started.
  2. I'll pull the day's total sales from the point of sale system.
  3. I'll pull total hours worked and labor cost from the point of sale system's time clock.
  4. I'll calculate labor cost as a percentage of sales.
  5. I'll post the full breakdown in the management chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Daily Sales & Labor Summary: $6,135 in sales, 82.8 labor hrs, $1,194 in wages, 19.5% labor cost.

workflows.description: The moment someone asks me to turn a chaotic, back-and-forth group chat into to-dos, I scan the conversation and create one for each action item.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone asks me to turn this conversation into to-dos, I'll get started.
  2. I'll reread the whole thread to find decisions, commitments, and action items mentioned.
  3. I'll figure out who each action item belongs to, based on who volunteered or was assigned in the conversation.
  4. I'll create a separate to-do for each action item and assign it to the right person.
  5. I'll post a summary list in the team member chat so everyone can see what got assigned.
workflows.exampleMessage: Pulled 3 to-dos from this thread: Tables, Taylor M. Sound system, Sam W. Signs, unassigned, still needs an owner.

workflows.description: Flags inappropriate language or unauthorized file sharing in chat channels and alerts HR.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a message or file is posted in any chat channel, I'll get started.
  2. I'll scan the content against your policy for prohibited language and unauthorized file types.
  3. If something's flagged, I'll capture the message, sender, and channel it came from.
  4. I'll alert HR directly with those details, without reposting the flagged content publicly.
  5. I'll log the incident in the HR chat for record-keeping.
workflows.exampleMessage: Compliance flag: Liam C. posted profanity directed at a coworker in Site Crew, 11:54 PM. Sent to HR for review.

workflows.description: Sets up a to-do that repeats on whatever schedule you give it, and creates a new one automatically each time it comes around, like a to-do for the store manager to run the loss prevention audit, every Friday.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment you tell me to set up a recurring task, like "create a to-do for the store manager to run the loss prevention audit, every Friday", I'll get started.
  2. I'll set the recurrence rule in the calendar for every Friday.
  3. I'll create the first to-do right now and assign it to the store manager.
  4. From then on, every time the schedule comes around, I'll create a new to-do automatically and assign it the same way. You won't need to ask me again.
  5. I'll post each one in the team member chat as it's created, so it's visible right when it goes out.
workflows.exampleMessage: New recurring to-do created for the store manager: run the loss prevention audit. Repeats automatically every Friday, I'll create and assign it each time, no need to ask again.

workflows.description: Checks whether a reorder is already scheduled the moment any tracked item drops below its threshold, and places one with the supplier if not.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment any tracked item drops below the threshold you've set for it in the inventory system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the inventory system for whether a reorder is already scheduled or in transit.
  3. If nothing's scheduled, I'll check the preferred supplier and standard order quantity for that item.
  4. I'll place the order with the supplier at the standard quantity.
  5. I'll post the order confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Medium shipping boxes ran low (10 of 38 units left), no reorder was scheduled. Ordered one pallet of 500 from Uline.

workflows.description: Reminds staff to complete whatever prep steps are still outstanding before a scheduled pickup.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. A set number of minutes ahead of the scheduled pickup time, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check which required prep steps for that pickup haven't been marked complete yet.
  3. I'll check the schedule for who's on shift and responsible for that area.
  4. I'll remind them directly with exactly what's left to do and how much time remains.
  5. I'll post a status update in the team member chat once everything's confirmed done.
workflows.exampleMessage: Carrier pickup at 3:00 PM, 1 hour out: still need to stage and label the outbound orders. Reminder sent to Ryan O.

workflows.description: Looks up a purchase order's status the moment someone asks in chat, without needing to log into the ordering system.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone asks about a purchase order's status in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll find the PO number they mentioned, or their most recent open PO if they didn't give one.
  3. I'll check the inventory system for that PO's current status: ordered, shipped, or delivered.
  4. If it hasn't arrived yet, I'll check for an estimated delivery date.
  5. I'll reply directly in the chat with the status and date.
workflows.exampleMessage: PO #7194 shipped yesterday, estimated delivery tomorrow by noon.

workflows.description: Notifies managers the moment a staff member crosses into overtime hours.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a staff member's hours this week cross into overtime in the payroll software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check exactly how many overtime hours they've logged so far.
  3. I'll check their remaining scheduled shifts for the rest of the week.
  4. I'll notify their manager directly with the current overtime total and what's still scheduled.
  5. I'll post a summary in the leadership chat so it's visible beyond just that manager.
workflows.exampleMessage: Grace P. is in overtime: 42.9 hrs logged (2.9 OT), 2 shifts left this week. Sent to Jordan L.

workflows.description: Reads the transcription of any Zenzap call for action items, creates a to-do for each one assigned to whoever it belongs to, and takes on any it can complete itself.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a Zenzap call ends, I'll get started.
  2. I'll read the call transcription for action items and who each one was assigned to or volunteered for.
  3. I'll check each action item against what I can complete directly, like placing an order or setting a reminder, versus what needs a person.
  4. I'll create a to-do for every action item, assigning each one to the right person, and assigning myself the ones I can handle directly.
  5. I'll post the full list in the call's chat so everyone can see what got assigned, including what I'm taking care of myself.
workflows.exampleMessage: 3 action items from today's call: 1) Reorder shipping boxes, me, placing the order now. 2) Follow up with corporate about the return policy question, Chris B. 3) Update the holiday schedule, Grace P.

workflows.description: Reads a tech issue reported in chat, figures out urgency, and creates a ticket assigned to the right person.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone reports a tech issue in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the description to figure out urgency and which system it affects.
  3. I'll check the IT ticketing tool for who's on call or assigned to that system.
  4. I'll create a ticket in the IT ticketing tool and assign it to the right person.
  5. I'll post the ticket number and assignment in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Ticket #4774: Liam C.'s register won't scan barcodes, marked high priority. Assigned to Jordan L.

workflows.description: Routes a request for system access to the right approver, and grants or provisions it once approved.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone requests access to a system or tool in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check who owns approval for that system.
  3. I'll route the request to that approver and wait for a yes or no.
  4. Once approved, I'll grant the access directly if I'm able to, or open a ticket for IT to do it.
  5. I'll post the outcome in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: James K.'s request for the inventory system access approved by Grace P. Access granted.

workflows.description: Routes any expense over your approval threshold to the right approver before it's logged.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment an expense over your approval threshold is submitted in the accounting software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the amount against your approval thresholds to figure out who needs to sign off.
  3. I'll route the expense to that approver with the amount, vendor, and category.
  4. I'll wait for their approval or denial.
  5. I'll post the outcome in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: $2,693 expense from Sysco routed to Alex T. for approval (over the $500 threshold). Approved.

workflows.description: Flags any expense category that's approaching or has crossed its monthly budget.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check spending against budget in the accounting software.
  2. I'll check each category's spending against its monthly budget.
  3. I'll flag any category that's at or over 90% of budget.
  4. I'll calculate how much room is left and how many days remain in the month.
  5. I'll post the flagged categories in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Packaging Supplies spending is at 89% of this month's budget with 12 days left. $451 remaining.

workflows.description: Logs a safety incident reported in chat and routes it to the safety or compliance lead.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone reports a safety incident in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll capture the details: what happened, where, and who was involved.
  3. I'll check your policy for whether it needs to be logged formally or just tracked.
  4. I'll log the incident and route it to the safety or compliance lead.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the compliance chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Incident logged: James K. reported a minor cut requiring a bandage at 9:45 AM. Routed to Ryan O. for review.

workflows.description: Reminds the right person ahead of a contract or lease auto-renewal deadline.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check upcoming contract and lease renewal dates in the contract management system.
  2. I'll check which contracts are within 60 days of renewal or auto-renewal.
  3. I'll check whether anyone's already flagged it for review or cancellation.
  4. I'll remind the responsible person with the deadline and terms.
  5. I'll post a summary in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: The store lease auto-renews in 54 days ($10k/year). Reminder sent to Maria S.

workflows.description: Checks that the required documents are on file, then creates a new vendor in the accounting software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone requests a new vendor be added in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check whether the required documents (W9, certificate of insurance) have been attached.
  3. If anything's missing, I'll ask the requester directly for it.
  4. Once everything's in, I'll create the vendor in the accounting software.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Office Depot added to the accounting software. W9 and COI on file. Requested by Sam W.

workflows.description: Broadcasts an open shift to eligible staff the moment someone requests coverage, and assigns it to whoever claims it first.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone requests coverage for their shift in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the shift scheduling system for who's eligible and available to cover.
  3. I'll broadcast the open shift to eligible staff.
  4. I'll assign it to whoever claims it first and update the schedule.
  5. I'll post the update in the team member chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Maria S.'s Thursday closing shift covered by Chris B. Schedule updated.

workflows.description: Reads the bulk or wholesale order details someone writes in a Zenzap chat, structures the estimate (SKUs, quantities, discount tier) into a standard draft, and creates the quote in the CRM.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone writes scope details for a job in a Zenzap chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll extract the raw estimate details from what they wrote: SKUs, quantities, and discount tier.
  3. I'll structure those details into your standard quote format.
  4. I'll check your pricing sheet for the applicable rates.
  5. I'll create the quote in the CRM and post it back in the chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Wholesale quote drafted for 200 units across 3 SKUs at the tier-2 discount. Created in the CRM for review.

workflows.description: Tracks devices and equipment issued to staff, and flags anything overdue to be returned.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a device or piece of equipment is issued to someone, I'll get started.
  2. I'll log it in the asset management system under their name.
  3. I'll check the asset management system every week for anything overdue to be returned.
  4. I'll message whoever has an overdue item directly.
  5. I'll post a summary in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Ryan O.'s loaner laptop (Asset #A337) is 14 days overdue for return. Reminder sent.

workflows.description: Tracks upcoming software license renewal dates and reminds the right person before they lapse.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check upcoming software license renewal dates.
  2. I'll check which licenses renew in the next 30 days.
  3. I'll check whether the license is still actively in use.
  4. I'll remind the responsible person with the renewal date and cost.
  5. I'll post a summary in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: The inventory system license renews in 20 days ($8k/year). Reminder sent to Alex T.

workflows.description: Creates a to-do for every IT setup task a new hire needs, and assigns them to IT.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new hire's start date arrives in the HR system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check what accounts and equipment their role requires.
  3. I'll create a to-do for each IT setup task and assign it to IT.
  4. I'll confirm with IT once everything's provisioned.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: IT setup to-dos created for James K.: email account, system access, laptop. Assigned to Ashley B.

workflows.description: Reviews who has access to which systems every quarter and flags anything that looks outdated.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every quarter, I'll get started.
  2. I'll pull the current list of who has access to which systems.
  3. I'll check for anyone who's left or changed roles but still has access.
  4. I'll flag anything that looks outdated.
  5. I'll post the list in the IT chat for review.
workflows.exampleMessage: Quarterly access review: found 2 accounts with access tied to former roles (Ryan O., Taylor M.). Flagged for review.

workflows.description: Tracks which required new hire forms are still outstanding and follows up directly.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new hire is added in the HR system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check which required forms are still outstanding.
  3. I'll message the new hire directly with what's left to complete.
  4. I'll check again after 3 days if anything's still missing.
  5. I'll post a status update in the HR chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Ryan O. still needs to submit their I-9. Reminder sent, due in 1 days.

workflows.description: Pulls last week's key numbers from your connected tools and posts a short digest to leadership.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every Monday morning, I'll get started.
  2. I'll pull last week's key numbers from your connected tools.
  3. I'll compare them to the week before.
  4. I'll put together a short digest.
  5. I'll post it in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Weekly digest: revenue up 10% week over week, labor cost steady at 21%, 3 open compliance items.

workflows.description: Flags vendors with rising costs or repeated issues every quarter, and reminds leadership to review them.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every quarter, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check spending and any issues logged for your top vendors.
  3. I'll flag any vendor with repeated issues or rising costs.
  4. I'll remind leadership to review that vendor relationship.
  5. I'll post the list in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Quarterly vendor review: Uline flagged, costs up 11% with 2 late deliveryies logged.

workflows.description: Checks vendor compliance documents for expiration every month and requests updated copies.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every month, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check which vendors have expiring or missing compliance documents, like a W9 or certificate of insurance.
  3. I'll flag any vendor with an expired or missing document.
  4. I'll message that vendor's contact for an updated copy.
  5. I'll post the list in the compliance chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Sysco's certificate of insurance expired last week. Requested an updated copy.

workflows.description: The moment a quote is marked won in the CRM, creates the matching invoice in the accounting software automatically.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a quote is marked won in the CRM, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the CRM for the quote details: customer, line items, and total.
  3. I'll check the accounting software for that customer's existing account.
  4. I'll create the invoice in the accounting software with the same line items and total.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Quote #4369 for Karen Sullivan marked won in the CRM. Invoice #1969 created in the accounting software for $3,897.

workflows.description: The moment a reorder is placed in the inventory system, creates the matching pending expense entry in the accounting software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a reorder is placed in the inventory system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the inventory system for the item, quantity, and cost.
  3. I'll check the accounting software for the right expense category.
  4. I'll create a pending expense entry in the accounting software.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Reorder placed for shipping boxes ($457, Office Depot). Pending expense entry created in the accounting software under "Packaging Supplies."

workflows.description: The moment a new hire is added in the HR system, syncs their role and pay rate straight into the payroll software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new hire is added in the HR system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the HR system for their role, start date, and pay rate.
  3. I'll check the payroll software for whether they've already been set up.
  4. I'll create their payroll profile with the matching role and pay rate.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the HR chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Ryan O. added in the HR system as shift lead, $17/hr. Payroll profile created in the payroll software.

workflows.description: The moment a payment is marked received in the accounting software, updates the matching deal's status in the CRM.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a payment is marked received in the accounting software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the accounting software for which invoice and customer it's tied to.
  3. I'll check the CRM for the matching deal.
  4. I'll update that deal's status to "Paid" in the CRM.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Payment received for invoice #1047 ($12,742) in the accounting software. William Foster's deal status updated to "Paid" in the CRM.

workflows.description: Sets up a to-do that repeats on whatever schedule you give it, and creates a new one automatically each time it comes around, like a to-do for the facilities team to test the fire alarms, once a month.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment you tell me to set up a recurring task, like "create a to-do for the facilities team to test the fire alarms, once a month", I'll get started.
  2. I'll set the recurrence rule for once a month.
  3. I'll create the first to-do right now and assign it to the facilities team.
  4. From then on, every time the schedule comes around, I'll create a new to-do automatically and assign it the same way. You won't need to ask me again.
  5. I'll post each one in the operations chat as it's created, so it's visible right when it goes out.
workflows.exampleMessage: New recurring to-do created for the facilities team: test the fire alarms. Repeats automatically once a month, I'll create and assign it each time, no need to ask again.

workflows.description: Checks whether a reorder is already scheduled the moment any tracked item drops below its threshold, and places one with the supplier if not.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment any tracked item drops below the threshold you've set for it in the inventory system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the inventory system for whether a reorder is already scheduled or in transit.
  3. If nothing's scheduled, I'll check the preferred supplier and standard order quantity for that item.
  4. I'll place the order with the supplier at the standard quantity.
  5. I'll post the order confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Printer paper ran low (6 of 29 units left), no reorder was scheduled. Ordered one case from School Specialty.

workflows.description: Looks up a purchase order's status the moment someone asks in chat, without needing to log into the ordering system.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone asks about a purchase order's status in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll find the PO number they mentioned, or their most recent open PO if they didn't give one.
  3. I'll check the inventory system for that PO's current status: ordered, shipped, or delivered.
  4. If it hasn't arrived yet, I'll check for an estimated delivery date.
  5. I'll reply directly in the chat with the status and date.
workflows.exampleMessage: PO #5826 shipped yesterday, estimated delivery tomorrow by noon.

workflows.description: Notifies managers the moment a staff member crosses into overtime hours.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a staff member's hours this week cross into overtime in the payroll software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check exactly how many overtime hours they've logged so far.
  3. I'll check their remaining scheduled shifts for the rest of the week.
  4. I'll notify their manager directly with the current overtime total and what's still scheduled.
  5. I'll post a summary in the leadership chat so it's visible beyond just that manager.
workflows.exampleMessage: Nina D. is in overtime: 44.7 hrs logged (4.7 OT), 1 shift left this week. Sent to Maria S.

workflows.description: Reads the transcription of any Zenzap call for action items, creates a to-do for each one assigned to whoever it belongs to, and takes on any it can complete itself.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a Zenzap call ends, I'll get started.
  2. I'll read the call transcription for action items and who each one was assigned to or volunteered for.
  3. I'll check each action item against what I can complete directly, like placing an order or setting a reminder, versus what needs a person.
  4. I'll create a to-do for every action item, assigning each one to the right person, and assigning myself the ones I can handle directly.
  5. I'll post the full list in the call's chat so everyone can see what got assigned, including what I'm taking care of myself.
workflows.exampleMessage: 3 action items from today's call: 1) Order more art supplies, me, placing the order now. 2) Follow up with the substitute teacher pool, Chris B. 3) Update the field trip schedule, Maria S.

workflows.description: Reads a tech issue reported in chat, figures out urgency, and creates a ticket assigned to the right person.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone reports a tech issue in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the description to figure out urgency and which system it affects.
  3. I'll check the IT ticketing tool for who's on call or assigned to that system.
  4. I'll create a ticket in the IT ticketing tool and assign it to the right person.
  5. I'll post the ticket number and assignment in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Ticket #4274: Chris B.'s classroom projector won't connect, marked medium priority. Assigned to Jordan L.

workflows.description: Routes a request for system access to the right approver, and grants or provisions it once approved.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone requests access to a system or tool in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check who owns approval for that system.
  3. I'll route the request to that approver and wait for a yes or no.
  4. Once approved, I'll grant the access directly if I'm able to, or open a ticket for IT to do it.
  5. I'll post the outcome in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Nina D.'s request for the student information system access approved by Liam C. Access granted.

workflows.description: Routes any expense over your approval threshold to the right approver before it's logged.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment an expense over your approval threshold is submitted in the accounting software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the amount against your approval thresholds to figure out who needs to sign off.
  3. I'll route the expense to that approver with the amount, vendor, and category.
  4. I'll wait for their approval or denial.
  5. I'll post the outcome in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: $1,578 expense from Sysco routed to Nina D. for approval (over the $500 threshold). Approved.

workflows.description: Flags any expense category that's approaching or has crossed its monthly budget.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check spending against budget in the accounting software.
  2. I'll check each category's spending against its monthly budget.
  3. I'll flag any category that's at or over 90% of budget.
  4. I'll calculate how much room is left and how many days remain in the month.
  5. I'll post the flagged categories in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Classroom Supplies spending is at 98% of this month's budget with 5 days left. $883 remaining.

workflows.description: Tracks staff certifications and licenses nearing expiration, and reminds the person until it's renewed.
workflows.workflowHtml:

  2. I'll check which staff certifications or licenses expire in the next 30 days.
  3. I'll message each person directly with their expiration date and renewal steps.
  4. I'll create a to-do for each one so it's tracked until renewed.
  5. I'll post a summary in the compliance chat.

workflows.description: Logs a safety incident reported in chat and routes it to the safety or compliance lead.

workflows.useCase: Monthly Vendor Spend vs Stock Report
workflows.description: Checks both the accounting software and the inventory system every month to compare vendor spend against actual stock levels, catching overordering early.
workflows.workflowHtml:

  2. I'll check the accounting software for total spend by vendor last month.
  3. I'll check the inventory system for current stock levels for that vendor's items.
  4. I'll flag any vendor where spend is up but stock isn't moving.
  5. I'll post the report in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: SchoolMart Supply spend up 13% last month, but the inventory system shows stock barely moved. Flagged for review.

workflows.description: Extracts pricing details from any receipt photo, figures out the right expense category, and syncs it straight into the accounting software.

  2. I'll reread the whole thread to find decisions, commitments, and action items mentioned.
  3. I'll figure out who each action item belongs to, based on who volunteered or was assigned in the conversation.
  4. I'll create a separate to-do for each action item and assign it to the right person.
  5. I'll post a summary list in the team member chat so everyone can see what got assigned.

  3. If something's flagged, I'll capture the message, sender, and channel it came from.
  4. I'll alert HR directly with those details, without reposting the flagged content publicly.
  5. I'll log the incident in the HR chat for record-keeping.

  3. I'll create the first to-do right now and assign it to the front desk.
  4. From then on, every time the schedule comes around, I'll create a new to-do automatically and assign it the same way. You won't need to ask me again.
  5. I'll post each one in the team member chat as it's created, so it's visible right when it goes out.
workflows.exampleMessage: New recurring to-do created for the front desk: restock retail inventory. Repeats automatically once a month, I'll create and assign it each time, no need to ask again.

  4. I'll place the order with the supplier at the standard quantity.

  3. I'll message the new hire directly with a step-by-step walkthrough of company protocols.
  4. I'll create a separate to-do for every onboarding task and assign them all to the new hire.
workflows.exampleMessage: Welcome, Ashley B.! Here's your day one to-do list (3 tasks): 1) Complete required compliance training. 2) Review company handbook. 3) Confirm system access. All added to your to-dos, due by end of day.

workflows.description: Feeds daily sales and hours worked from the point of sale system straight into the management chat.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every day at close, I'll get started.
  2. I'll pull the day's total sales from the point of sale system.
  3. I'll pull total hours worked and labor cost from the point of sale system's time clock.
  4. I'll calculate labor cost as a percentage of sales.
  5. I'll post the full breakdown in the management chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Daily Sales & Labor Summary: $3,216 in sales, 43.6 labor hrs, $657 in wages, 20.4% labor cost.

workflows.description: The moment someone asks me to turn a chaotic, back-and-forth group chat into to-dos, I scan the conversation and create one for each action item.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone asks me to turn this conversation into to-dos, I'll get started.
  2. I'll reread the whole thread to find decisions, commitments, and action items mentioned.
  3. I'll figure out who each action item belongs to, based on who volunteered or was assigned in the conversation.
  4. I'll create a separate to-do for each action item and assign it to the right person.
  5. I'll post a summary list in the team member chat so everyone can see what got assigned.
workflows.exampleMessage: Pulled 3 to-dos from this thread: Tables, Maria S. Sound system, Chris B. Signs, unassigned, still needs an owner.

workflows.description: Flags inappropriate language or unauthorized file sharing in chat channels and alerts HR.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a message or file is posted in any chat channel, I'll get started.
  2. I'll scan the content against your policy for prohibited language and unauthorized file types.
  3. If something's flagged, I'll capture the message, sender, and channel it came from.
  4. I'll alert HR directly with those details, without reposting the flagged content publicly.
  5. I'll log the incident in the HR chat for record-keeping.
workflows.exampleMessage: Compliance flag: Maria S. shared a screenshot of payroll records outside the finance channel in Store Team, 1:57 PM. Sent to HR for review.

workflows.description: Sets up a to-do that repeats on whatever schedule you give it, and creates a new one automatically each time it comes around, like a to-do for the ops manager to check the fire extinguishers, once a month.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment you tell me to set up a recurring task, like "create a to-do for the ops manager to check the fire extinguishers, once a month", I'll get started.
  2. I'll set the recurrence rule for once a month.
  3. I'll create the first to-do right now and assign it to the ops manager.
  4. From then on, every time the schedule comes around, I'll create a new to-do automatically and assign it the same way. You won't need to ask me again.
  5. I'll post each one in the operations chat as it's created, so it's visible right when it goes out.
workflows.exampleMessage: New recurring to-do created for the ops manager: check the fire extinguishers. Repeats automatically once a month, I'll create and assign it each time, no need to ask again.

workflows.description: Checks whether a reorder is already scheduled the moment any tracked item drops below its threshold, and places one with the supplier if not.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment any tracked item drops below the threshold you've set for it in the inventory system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the inventory system for whether a reorder is already scheduled or in transit.
  3. If nothing's scheduled, I'll check the preferred supplier and standard order quantity for that item.
  4. I'll place the order with the supplier at the standard quantity.
  5. I'll post the order confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Printer toner ran low (6 of 29 units left), no reorder was scheduled. Ordered one twin pack from Office Depot.

workflows.description: Reminds staff to complete whatever prep steps are still outstanding before a scheduled pickup.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. A set number of minutes ahead of the scheduled pickup time, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check which required prep steps for that pickup haven't been marked complete yet.
  3. I'll check the schedule for who's on shift and responsible for that area.
  4. I'll remind them directly with exactly what's left to do and how much time remains.
  5. I'll post a status update in the team member chat once everything's confirmed done.
workflows.exampleMessage: Scheduled pickup at the scheduled time, 1 hour out: still need to complete the required prep steps. Reminder sent to Nina D.

workflows.description: Marks a job complete the moment a team member finishes it and assigns them the next priority job nearby.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a team member marks their current job complete in the field service software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the job queue for the next unassigned priority job.
  3. I'll check that team member's current location against nearby job addresses to find the closest match.
  4. I'll assign the next job to that team member in the field service software.
  5. I'll message them directly with the new job's address and details, and post the assignment in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Liam C. finished Elm St, now assigned to 214 Oak Ave (clogged drain, priority, 1.5 miles away).

workflows.description: Looks up a purchase order's status the moment someone asks in chat, without needing to log into the ordering system.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone asks about a purchase order's status in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll find the PO number they mentioned, or their most recent open PO if they didn't give one.
  3. I'll check the inventory system for that PO's current status: ordered, shipped, or delivered.
  4. If it hasn't arrived yet, I'll check for an estimated delivery date.
  5. I'll reply directly in the chat with the status and date.
workflows.exampleMessage: PO #3621 shipped yesterday, estimated delivery tomorrow by noon.

workflows.description: Notifies managers the moment a staff member crosses into overtime hours.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a staff member's hours this week cross into overtime in the payroll software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check exactly how many overtime hours they've logged so far.
  3. I'll check their remaining scheduled shifts for the rest of the week.
  4. I'll notify their manager directly with the current overtime total and what's still scheduled.
  5. I'll post a summary in the leadership chat so it's visible beyond just that manager.
workflows.exampleMessage: Sam W. is in overtime: 43.7 hrs logged (3.7 OT), 3 shifts left this week. Sent to Liam C.

workflows.description: Reads the transcription of any Zenzap call for action items, creates a to-do for each one assigned to whoever it belongs to, and takes on any it can complete itself.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a Zenzap call ends, I'll get started.
  2. I'll read the call transcription for action items and who each one was assigned to or volunteered for.
  3. I'll check each action item against what I can complete directly, like placing an order or setting a reminder, versus what needs a person.
  4. I'll create a to-do for every action item, assigning each one to the right person, and assigning myself the ones I can handle directly.
  5. I'll post the full list in the call's chat so everyone can see what got assigned, including what I'm taking care of myself.
workflows.exampleMessage: 3 action items from today's call: 1) Reorder printer toner, me, placing the order now. 2) Follow up with a vendor about an invoice, Jordan L. 3) Update the team calendar, Grace P.

workflows.description: Reads a tech issue reported in chat, figures out urgency, and creates a ticket assigned to the right person.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone reports a tech issue in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the description to figure out urgency and which system it affects.
  3. I'll check the IT ticketing tool for who's on call or assigned to that system.
  4. I'll create a ticket in the IT ticketing tool and assign it to the right person.
  5. I'll post the ticket number and assignment in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Ticket #4945: Maria S.'s laptop won't connect to Wi-Fi, marked medium priority. Assigned to Sam W.

workflows.description: Routes a request for system access to the right approver, and grants or provisions it once approved.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone requests access to a system or tool in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check who owns approval for that system.
  3. I'll route the request to that approver and wait for a yes or no.
  4. Once approved, I'll grant the access directly if I'm able to, or open a ticket for IT to do it.
  5. I'll post the outcome in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Sam W.'s request for the shared drive access approved by Chris B. Access granted.

workflows.description: Routes any expense over your approval threshold to the right approver before it's logged.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment an expense over your approval threshold is submitted in the accounting software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the amount against your approval thresholds to figure out who needs to sign off.
  3. I'll route the expense to that approver with the amount, vendor, and category.
  4. I'll wait for their approval or denial.
  5. I'll post the outcome in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: $3,770 expense from Sherwin-Williams routed to Maria S. for approval (over the $500 threshold). Approved.

workflows.description: Flags any expense category that's approaching or has crossed its monthly budget.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check spending against budget in the accounting software.
  2. I'll check each category's spending against its monthly budget.
  3. I'll flag any category that's at or over 90% of budget.
  4. I'll calculate how much room is left and how many days remain in the month.
  5. I'll post the flagged categories in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Office Supplies spending is at 90% of this month's budget with 8 days left. $354 remaining.

workflows.description: Tracks staff certifications and licenses nearing expiration, and reminds the person until it's renewed.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check upcoming certification and license expirations in the HR system.
  2. I'll check which staff certifications or licenses expire in the next 30 days.
  3. I'll message each person directly with their expiration date and renewal steps.
  4. I'll create a to-do for each one so it's tracked until renewed.
  5. I'll post a summary in the compliance chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Grace P.'s required certification expires in 16 days. Reminder sent, to-do created.

workflows.description: Logs a safety incident reported in chat and routes it to the safety or compliance lead.
workflows.workflowHtml:

  2. I'll capture the details: what happened, where, and who was involved.
  3. I'll check your policy for whether it needs to be logged formally or just tracked.
  4. I'll log the incident and route it to the safety or compliance lead.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the compliance chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Incident logged: Ashley B. reported a slip near the walk-in, no injury at 10:18 AM. Routed to Ryan O. for review.

workflows.description: Reminds the right person ahead of a contract or lease auto-renewal deadline.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check upcoming contract and lease renewal dates in the contract management system.
  2. I'll check which contracts are within 60 days of renewal or auto-renewal.
  3. I'll check whether anyone's already flagged it for review or cancellation.
  4. I'll remind the responsible person with the deadline and terms.
  5. I'll post a summary in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: The office lease auto-renews in 48 days ($5k/year). Reminder sent to Grace P.

workflows.description: Checks that the required documents are on file, then creates a new vendor in the accounting software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone requests a new vendor be added in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check whether the required documents (W9, certificate of insurance) have been attached.
  3. If anything's missing, I'll ask the requester directly for it.
  4. Once everything's in, I'll create the vendor in the accounting software.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Uline added to the accounting software. W9 and COI on file. Requested by Grace P.

workflows.description: Reads the scope details someone writes in a Zenzap chat, structures the raw estimate into a standard draft, and creates the quote in the CRM.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone writes scope details for a job in a Zenzap chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll extract the raw estimate details from what they wrote.
  3. I'll structure those details into your standard quote format.
  4. I'll check your pricing sheet for the applicable rates.
  5. I'll create the quote in the CRM and post it back in the chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Quote drafted from chat scope details and created in the CRM for review.

workflows.description: Tracks devices and equipment issued to staff, and flags anything overdue to be returned.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a device or piece of equipment is issued to someone, I'll get started.
  2. I'll log it in the asset management system under their name.
  3. I'll check the asset management system every week for anything overdue to be returned.
  4. I'll message whoever has an overdue item directly.
  5. I'll post a summary in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Ryan O.'s loaner laptop (Asset #A337) is 16 days overdue for return. Reminder sent.

workflows.description: Tracks upcoming software license renewal dates and reminds the right person before they lapse.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check upcoming software license renewal dates.
  2. I'll check which licenses renew in the next 30 days.
  3. I'll check whether the license is still actively in use.
  4. I'll remind the responsible person with the renewal date and cost.
  5. I'll post a summary in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: The office software license renews in 25 days ($19k/year). Reminder sent to Liam C.

workflows.description: Creates a to-do for every IT setup task a new hire needs, and assigns them to IT.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new hire's start date arrives in the HR system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check what accounts and equipment their role requires.
  3. I'll create a to-do for each IT setup task and assign it to IT.
  4. I'll confirm with IT once everything's provisioned.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: IT setup to-dos created for James K.: email account, system access, laptop. Assigned to Sam W.

workflows.description: Reviews who has access to which systems every quarter and flags anything that looks outdated.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every quarter, I'll get started.
  2. I'll pull the current list of who has access to which systems.
  3. I'll check for anyone who's left or changed roles but still has access.
  4. I'll flag anything that looks outdated.
  5. I'll post the list in the IT chat for review.
workflows.exampleMessage: Quarterly access review: found 2 accounts with access tied to former roles (Chris B., Maria S.). Flagged for review.

workflows.description: Tracks which required new hire forms are still outstanding and follows up directly.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new hire is added in the HR system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check which required forms are still outstanding.
  3. I'll message the new hire directly with what's left to complete.
  4. I'll check again after 3 days if anything's still missing.
  5. I'll post a status update in the HR chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Liam C. still needs to submit their W-4. Reminder sent, due in 2 days.

workflows.description: Pulls last week's key numbers from your connected tools and posts a short digest to leadership.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every Monday morning, I'll get started.
  2. I'll pull last week's key numbers from your connected tools.
  3. I'll compare them to the week before.
  4. I'll put together a short digest.
  5. I'll post it in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Weekly digest: revenue up 7% week over week, labor cost steady at 21%, 0 open compliance items.

workflows.description: Flags vendors with rising costs or repeated issues every quarter, and reminds leadership to review them.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every quarter, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check spending and any issues logged for your top vendors.
  3. I'll flag any vendor with repeated issues or rising costs.
  4. I'll remind leadership to review that vendor relationship.
  5. I'll post the list in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Quarterly vendor review: Office Depot flagged, costs up 11% with 3 late deliveryies logged.

workflows.description: Checks vendor compliance documents for expiration every month and requests updated copies.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every month, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check which vendors have expiring or missing compliance documents, like a W9 or certificate of insurance.
  3. I'll flag any vendor with an expired or missing document.
  4. I'll message that vendor's contact for an updated copy.
  5. I'll post the list in the compliance chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Sherwin-Williams's certificate of insurance expired last week. Requested an updated copy.

workflows.description: The moment a quote is marked won in the CRM, creates the matching invoice in the accounting software automatically.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a quote is marked won in the CRM, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the CRM for the quote details: customer, line items, and total.
  3. I'll check the accounting software for that customer's existing account.
  4. I'll create the invoice in the accounting software with the same line items and total.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Quote #4134 for Susan Patel marked won in the CRM. Invoice #1849 created in the accounting software for $7,143.

workflows.description: The moment a reorder is placed in the inventory system, creates the matching pending expense entry in the accounting software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a reorder is placed in the inventory system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the inventory system for the item, quantity, and cost.
  3. I'll check the accounting software for the right expense category.
  4. I'll create a pending expense entry in the accounting software.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Reorder placed for printer toner ($408, Uline). Pending expense entry created in the accounting software under "Office Supplies."

workflows.description: The moment a new hire is added in the HR system, syncs their role and pay rate straight into the payroll software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new hire is added in the HR system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the HR system for their role, start date, and pay rate.
  3. I'll check the payroll software for whether they've already been set up.
  4. I'll create their payroll profile with the matching role and pay rate.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the HR chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Liam C. added in the HR system as front desk staff, $25/hr. Payroll profile created in the payroll software.

workflows.description: The moment parts are logged as used on a job in the field service software, deducts them from the inventory system, and reorders automatically if that drops it below threshold.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment parts are logged as used on a job in the field service software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the field service software for which parts and how many were used.
  3. I'll deduct that quantity from the inventory system.
  4. I'll check whether that drops the item below its reorder threshold.
  5. If it does, I'll place the reorder and post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Chris B. logged 5 circuit breakers used on Job #2015. Deducted from inventory system, now at 4 units, below the 6-unit threshold. Reorder placed.

workflows.description: The moment a payment is marked received in the accounting software, updates the matching deal's status in the CRM.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a payment is marked received in the accounting software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the accounting software for which invoice and customer it's tied to.
  3. I'll check the CRM for the matching deal.
  4. I'll update that deal's status to "Paid" in the CRM.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Payment received for invoice #1664 ($5,363) in the accounting software. Karen Sullivan's deal status updated to "Paid" in the CRM.

workflows.description: The moment a job is marked complete in the field service software, updates the matching project's status in the CRM.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a job is marked complete in the field service software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the field service software for which job and customer it's tied to.
  3. I'll check the CRM for the matching project or deal.
  4. I'll update that record's status to "Completed" in the CRM.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Job #2372 marked complete in the field service software. Karen Sullivan's project status updated to "Completed" in the CRM.

workflows.description: Checks both the CRM and the accounting software every week to compare revenue booked against cash actually collected.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every Monday morning, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the CRM for total revenue booked this week.
  3. I'll check the accounting software for total cash actually collected this week.
  4. I'll calculate the gap between booked and collected.
  5. I'll post the snapshot in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Weekly snapshot: $23,318 booked in the CRM, $21,185 collected in the accounting software. $2,133 still outstanding.

workflows.useCase: Monthly Vendor Spend vs Stock Report

workflows.workflowHtml:

  3. I'll check the inventory system for current stock levels for that vendor's items.
  4. I'll flag any vendor where spend is up but stock isn't moving.
  5. I'll post the report in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Summit Supply Co. spend up 18% last month, but the inventory system shows stock barely moved. Flagged for review.

  4. I'll create the expense entry in the accounting software under that category.
  5. I'll post a confirmation in the operations chat, tagging whoever submitted the receipt.
workflows.exampleMessage: Logged $649.30 from Regional Supply Partners (napkins and to-go boxes) as "Unit Supplies." @Chris, flag me if that category's not right.

  4. I'll send it as individual to-dos to each of the on-shift staff at each location coming on shift.
  5. I'll post it in the team member chat so the whole shift can see what's assigned.

workflows.description: Messages new hires on their first day to walk them through brand standards and safety protocols, and creates a to-do for each onboarding task so nothing gets missed.

workflows.exampleMessage: PO #4730 shipped yesterday, estimated delivery tomorrow by noon.

workflows.description: Notifies managers the moment a staff member crosses into overtime hours.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a staff member's hours this week cross into overtime in the payroll software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check exactly how many overtime hours they've logged so far.
  3. I'll check their remaining scheduled shifts for the rest of the week.
  4. I'll notify their manager directly with the current overtime total and what's still scheduled.
  5. I'll post a summary in the leadership chat so it's visible beyond just that manager.
workflows.exampleMessage: Liam C. is in overtime: 42.5 hrs logged (2.5 OT), 1 shift left this week. Sent to Taylor M.

workflows.description: Reads the transcription of any Zenzap call for action items, creates a to-do for each one assigned to whoever it belongs to, and takes on any it can complete itself.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a Zenzap call ends, I'll get started.
  2. I'll read the call transcription for action items and who each one was assigned to or volunteered for.
  3. I'll check each action item against what I can complete directly, like placing an order or setting a reminder, versus what needs a person.
  4. I'll create a to-do for every action item, assigning each one to the right person, and assigning myself the ones I can handle directly.
  5. I'll post the full list in the call's chat so everyone can see what got assigned, including what I'm taking care of myself.
workflows.exampleMessage: 3 action items from today's call: 1) Reorder to-go containers for the location, me, placing the order now. 2) Follow up with a franchisee about their compliance checklist, Nina D. 3) Confirm the new unit's opening date, Liam C.

workflows.description: Reads a tech issue reported in chat, figures out urgency, and creates a ticket assigned to the right person.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone reports a tech issue in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the description to figure out urgency and which system it affects.
  3. I'll check the IT ticketing tool for who's on call or assigned to that system.
  4. I'll create a ticket in the IT ticketing tool and assign it to the right person.
  5. I'll post the ticket number and assignment in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Ticket #4928: Maria S.'s POS terminal frozen, marked high priority. Assigned to Ryan O.

workflows.description: Routes a request for system access to the right approver, and grants or provisions it once approved.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone requests access to a system or tool in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check who owns approval for that system.
  3. I'll route the request to that approver and wait for a yes or no.
  4. Once approved, I'll grant the access directly if I'm able to, or open a ticket for IT to do it.
  5. I'll post the outcome in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Chris B.'s request for the franchise reporting system access approved by Ashley B. Access granted.

workflows.description: Routes any expense over your approval threshold to the right approver before it's logged.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment an expense over your approval threshold is submitted in the accounting software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the amount against your approval thresholds to figure out who needs to sign off.
  3. I'll route the expense to that approver with the amount, vendor, and category.
  4. I'll wait for their approval or denial.
  5. I'll post the outcome in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: $2,142 expense from Uline routed to Jordan L. for approval (over the $500 threshold). Approved.

workflows.description: Flags any expense category that's approaching or has crossed its monthly budget.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check spending against budget in the accounting software.
  2. I'll check each category's spending against its monthly budget.
  3. I'll flag any category that's at or over 90% of budget.
  4. I'll calculate how much room is left and how many days remain in the month.
  5. I'll post the flagged categories in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Unit Supplies spending is at 90% of this month's budget with 11 days left. $798 remaining.

workflows.description: Tracks staff certifications and licenses nearing expiration, and reminds the person until it's renewed.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check upcoming certification and license expirations in the HR system.
  2. I'll check which staff certifications or licenses expire in the next 30 days.
  3. I'll message each person directly with their expiration date and renewal steps.
  4. I'll create a to-do for each one so it's tracked until renewed.
  5. I'll post a summary in the compliance chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Taylor M.'s brand certification expires in 12 days. Reminder sent, to-do created.

workflows.description: Logs a safety incident reported in chat and routes it to the safety or compliance lead.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone reports a safety incident in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll capture the details: what happened, where, and who was involved.
  3. I'll check your policy for whether it needs to be logged formally or just tracked.
  4. I'll log the incident and route it to the safety or compliance lead.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the compliance chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Incident logged: Grace P. reported a near-miss with a forklift at 11:29 PM. Routed to Ashley B. for review.

workflows.description: Reminds the right person ahead of a contract or lease auto-renewal deadline.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check upcoming contract and lease renewal dates in the contract management system.
  2. I'll check which contracts are within 60 days of renewal or auto-renewal.
  3. I'll check whether anyone's already flagged it for review or cancellation.
  4. I'll remind the responsible person with the deadline and terms.
  5. I'll post a summary in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: The franchise agreement auto-renews in 54 days ($40k/year). Reminder sent to Ryan O.

workflows.description: Checks that the required documents are on file, then creates a new vendor in the accounting software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone requests a new vendor be added in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check whether the required documents (W9, certificate of insurance) have been attached.
  3. If anything's missing, I'll ask the requester directly for it.
  4. Once everything's in, I'll create the vendor in the accounting software.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Summit Supply Co. added to the accounting software. W9 and COI on file. Requested by Alex T.

workflows.description: Broadcasts an open shift to eligible staff the moment someone requests coverage, and assigns it to whoever claims it first.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone requests coverage for their shift in chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the shift scheduling system for who's eligible and available to cover.
  3. I'll broadcast the open shift to eligible staff.
  4. I'll assign it to whoever claims it first and update the schedule.
  5. I'll post the update in the team member chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Nina D.'s Monday closing shift covered by Grace P. Schedule updated.

workflows.description: Reads the scope details someone writes in a Zenzap chat, structures the raw estimate into a standard draft, and creates the quote in the CRM.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment someone writes scope details for a job in a Zenzap chat, I'll get started.
  2. I'll extract the raw estimate details from what they wrote.
  3. I'll structure those details into your standard quote format.
  4. I'll check your pricing sheet for the applicable rates.
  5. I'll create the quote in the CRM and post it back in the chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Quote drafted from chat scope details and created in the CRM for review.

workflows.description: Tracks devices and equipment issued to staff, and flags anything overdue to be returned.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a device or piece of equipment is issued to someone, I'll get started.
  2. I'll log it in the asset management system under their name.
  3. I'll check the asset management system every week for anything overdue to be returned.
  4. I'll message whoever has an overdue item directly.
  5. I'll post a summary in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Sam W.'s loaner laptop (Asset #A337) is 14 days overdue for return. Reminder sent.

workflows.description: Tracks upcoming software license renewal dates and reminds the right person before they lapse.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every week, I'll check upcoming software license renewal dates.
  2. I'll check which licenses renew in the next 30 days.
  3. I'll check whether the license is still actively in use.
  4. I'll remind the responsible person with the renewal date and cost.
  5. I'll post a summary in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: The franchise reporting system license renews in 28 days ($6k/year). Reminder sent to Ryan O.

workflows.description: Creates a to-do for every IT setup task a new hire needs, and assigns them to IT.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new hire's start date arrives in the HR system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check what accounts and equipment their role requires.
  3. I'll create a to-do for each IT setup task and assign it to IT.
  4. I'll confirm with IT once everything's provisioned.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the IT chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: IT setup to-dos created for Alex T.: email account, system access, laptop. Assigned to Maria S.

workflows.description: Reviews who has access to which systems every quarter and flags anything that looks outdated.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every quarter, I'll get started.
  2. I'll pull the current list of who has access to which systems.
  3. I'll check for anyone who's left or changed roles but still has access.
  4. I'll flag anything that looks outdated.
  5. I'll post the list in the IT chat for review.
workflows.exampleMessage: Quarterly access review: found 2 accounts with access tied to former roles (Liam C., Alex T.). Flagged for review.

workflows.description: Tracks which required new hire forms are still outstanding and follows up directly.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new hire is added in the HR system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check which required forms are still outstanding.
  3. I'll message the new hire directly with what's left to complete.
  4. I'll check again after 3 days if anything's still missing.
  5. I'll post a status update in the HR chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Chris B. still needs to submit their W-4. Reminder sent, due in 3 days.

workflows.description: Pulls last week's key numbers from your connected tools and posts a short digest to leadership.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every Monday morning, I'll get started.
  2. I'll pull last week's key numbers from your connected tools.
  3. I'll compare them to the week before.
  4. I'll put together a short digest.
  5. I'll post it in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Weekly digest: revenue up 5% week over week, labor cost steady at 16%, 1 open compliance items.

workflows.description: Flags vendors with rising costs or repeated issues every quarter, and reminds leadership to review them.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every quarter, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check spending and any issues logged for your top vendors.
  3. I'll flag any vendor with repeated issues or rising costs.
  4. I'll remind leadership to review that vendor relationship.
  5. I'll post the list in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Quarterly vendor review: Regional Supply Partners flagged, costs up 14% with 3 late deliveryies logged.

workflows.description: Checks vendor compliance documents for expiration every month and requests updated copies.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every month, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check which vendors have expiring or missing compliance documents, like a W9 or certificate of insurance.
  3. I'll flag any vendor with an expired or missing document.
  4. I'll message that vendor's contact for an updated copy.
  5. I'll post the list in the compliance chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Summit Supply Co.'s certificate of insurance expired last week. Requested an updated copy.

workflows.description: The moment a quote is marked won in the CRM, creates the matching invoice in the accounting software automatically.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a quote is marked won in the CRM, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the CRM for the quote details: customer, line items, and total.
  3. I'll check the accounting software for that customer's existing account.
  4. I'll create the invoice in the accounting software with the same line items and total.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Quote #4075 for Susan Patel marked won in the CRM. Invoice #1955 created in the accounting software for $6,910.

workflows.description: The moment a reorder is placed in the inventory system, creates the matching pending expense entry in the accounting software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a reorder is placed in the inventory system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the inventory system for the item, quantity, and cost.
  3. I'll check the accounting software for the right expense category.
  4. I'll create a pending expense entry in the accounting software.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Reorder placed for to-go containers ($560, Uline). Pending expense entry created in the accounting software under "Unit Supplies."

workflows.description: The moment a new hire is added in the HR system, syncs their role and pay rate straight into the payroll software.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a new hire is added in the HR system, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the HR system for their role, start date, and pay rate.
  3. I'll check the payroll software for whether they've already been set up.
  4. I'll create their payroll profile with the matching role and pay rate.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the HR chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: James K. added in the HR system as shift lead, $17/hr. Payroll profile created in the payroll software.

workflows.description: The moment a payment is marked received in the accounting software, updates the matching deal's status in the CRM.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. The moment a payment is marked received in the accounting software, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the accounting software for which invoice and customer it's tied to.
  3. I'll check the CRM for the matching deal.
  4. I'll update that deal's status to "Paid" in the CRM.
  5. I'll post confirmation in the operations chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Payment received for invoice #1951 ($2,286) in the accounting software. Barbara Nguyen's deal status updated to "Paid" in the CRM.

workflows.description: Checks both the CRM and the accounting software every week to compare revenue booked against cash actually collected.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. Every Monday morning, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the CRM for total revenue booked this week.
  3. I'll check the accounting software for total cash actually collected this week.
  4. I'll calculate the gap between booked and collected.
  5. I'll post the snapshot in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Weekly snapshot: $34,899 booked in the CRM, $31,261 collected in the accounting software. $3,638 still outstanding.

workflows.useCase: Monthly Vendor Spend vs Stock Report
workflows.description: Checks both the accounting software and the inventory system every month to compare vendor spend against actual stock levels, catching overordering early.
workflows.workflowHtml:
1. On the 1st of every month, I'll get started.
  2. I'll check the accounting software for total spend by vendor last month.
  3. I'll check the inventory system for current stock levels for that vendor's items.
  4. I'll flag any vendor where spend is up but stock isn't moving.
  5. I'll post the report in the leadership chat.
workflows.exampleMessage: Uline spend up 20% last month, but the inventory system shows stock barely moved. Flagged for review.
